what_happened: Scene: grey kettle on the counter right of a gas hob (pan on the hob); same layout as s0/s3/s13/s18/s20/s26. Stage 0: the gripper came down over the kettle 104-128. In the wrist view the handle lies flat across the kettle top, along the finger-closing direction. The fingers touched it only at 122-123 (packet 'hold' 122-124, lift 0), and by ~136 the gripper rose again without the kettle. 200-240 the arm swung over the hob and pan with an empty gripper. From ~280 to the end it hovered 20-30 cm above or beside the kettle, which stays centred in the wrist view at 640, 720, 800, 880 and 960, and it never came down again (no contact after 123, min_eef 0.16 m). The kettle never moved (0.1 cm). No knob was touched, and stage 1 was never reached.
causal_chain: handle lying along the closing axis at approach (104-128) -> 2-step touch 122-123, no lift -> gripper left (~136), empty-handed trip over the hob (200-240) -> hovered above the kettle 280-1000 with no second grasp attempt -> kettle still on the counter at timeout (1000); stage 0 never complete
self_recovery: Came back above the kettle at ~280 and stayed there ~700 steps but never descended to re-grasp; no effective recovery.
official_criterion_notes: The 2-step contact 122-124 is listed under 'holds' (lift 0.0); it is a touch, not a grasp. Official labeler segments are meaningless here (no pick segment).

packet_facts: stove: no gripper touch, all knobs 0.0

uncertain_about: Why the closure missed: 'handle lying along the closing axis' is my reading of 4-step wrist frames; finger-handle contact geometry is not visible. Also unclear why the policy never re-descended in 860 steps.
